chunks: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Farra' narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said:
A man from among our companions said to him: “Sometimes the time becomes unclear to us on a cloudy day.”
He said: “Do you know these birds that are with you in Iraq, which are called roosters?”
He said: “When their voices rise and they answer one another, then at that time perform salat (prayer).”

key_terms.الصَّادِقِ: Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الطُّيُورَ: the birds mentioned as natural indicators
key_terms.يَوْمِ غَيْمٍ: a cloudy day when normal visual signs are obscured

ai.seo_question: How should one determine the time of salat (prayer) on a cloudy day when the usual signs are unclear?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a practical indicator for determining the time of salat (prayer) when the sky is cloudy and the time is unclear. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام directs the questioner to observe the natural behavior of roosters as a sign for prayer time.
